foodDescription: A smoked pork sausage with garlic and pepper, protected by EU rules since 2015. Served with mustard, horseradish, and bread.
Rolled dough filled with cottage cheese, tarragon, walnuts, or other fillings, boiled or baked. There are said to be more than 70 kinds.
Small dumplings filled with potato, onion, and herbs, from the mining town of Idrija. Usually served with a lamb sauce.
A thick soup of beans, sauerkraut, and potatoes, often with smoked pork. Winter food from the west of the country.
A hearty stew of barley, beans, and smoked meat. Simple, filling, and found in every gostilna.
Buckwheat flour cooked into crumbly lumps and topped with cracklings. Once a farm breakfast, now a dish of national pride.
A rolled yeast cake with a spiral of walnut filling, baked for Christmas and Easter. Tarragon and poppy seed versions are common.
A rich layered cake of poppy seeds, cottage cheese, walnuts, and apples, from Prekmurje in the far northeast.
A thick slice of vanilla custard and cream between layers of pastry, made famous in Bled. Found in cafés all over the country.
The Balkan pastry, sold from late-night shops near the center. Ljubljana’s classic snack after a night out.
Lager from the Union brewery, founded in Ljubljana in 1864, the city’s side of a long rivalry with Laško beer.
A dark, acidic red wine from the Karst region near the coast, made from the Refošk grape. Often paired with pršut, the local dry-cured ham.
